title: Multiplexers in Front of the ALU: What Can Reach Each Input
unit: Design of the Arithmetic and Logic Unit
quickIdea: The ALU does not care where its operands come from. A multiplexer on each input decides that, and because the two select lines are independent, the datapath can be fed register-register, register-immediate or immediate-immediate.
remember: One multiplexer per ALU input, each with its own select line, unless the design deliberately ties them together.
Two independent 2:1 multiplexers give 2 x 2 = 4 operand-source combinations, not 2.
The ALU's function code and the input multiplexers' select lines are separate control fields; one says what to compute, the other says what to compute it on.
The register file is read first, so a register operand and an immediate operand can both be available in the same cycle - that is what makes a single-cycle datapath possible.
An immediate field is extended to the word width before it reaches the multiplexer, so the ALU always sees two n-bit values.

example.prompt: A datapath has Mux_A choosing between register RA and a 32-bit immediate, and Mux_B choosing between register RB and a 32-bit immediate. Which operand combinations can the ALU be given?
example.work: Each multiplexer has two settings and they are controlled independently, so the pairs are (RA, RB), (RA, imm), (imm, RB) and (imm, imm). All four are electrically possible; whether a compiler would ever emit the last one is a different question.
example.answer: All four combinations, which is 2 x 2 = 4, including two immediates at once.

gateAngle: This is GATE CSE 2025 Set 1 Q.27, an MSQ whose answer is A, B and C: two registers, one register with one immediate, and two immediates are all implementable. Option D fails only because of the word 'only'. The question rewards reading the two select lines as independent, and the common error is to assume a hardware design must be useful as well as possible.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: The two input multiplexers share one select line instead of having one each. How many operand combinations remain?
variations.why: One select line makes the choices correlated, which is exactly the case the 2025 question does not describe.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does an immediate need sign- or zero-extension before the ALU sees it?
variations.answer: Because the ALU is n bits wide and the immediate field is narrower; an unextended field would leave the upper bits undefined.
variations.why: This is the same width rule as the block contract, applied at the input instead of the output.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: Each ALU input multiplexer is 4:1 rather than 2:1. How many select bits does each need, and how many operand-source combinations exist?
variations.answer: Two select bits each, and 4 x 4 = 16 combinations.
variations.why: The count of combinations multiplies; the select bits add, 2 + 2 = 4 in all.

trap.what: Reading 'can implement' as 'is designed to be used for'.
trap.why: A datapath question asks what the wiring makes possible, not what a compiler would generate.
trap.counterexample: Two immediates added together is a pointless instruction, yet the hardware performs it happily - and that is why option C of the 2025 question is correct.

check.question: Two independent 2:1 multiplexers feed the ALU. If each select line is one bit, how many distinct control settings exist for the pair?
check.explanation: One bit per multiplexer, so the pair is a two-bit control field. The trap is answering two, one per multiplexer.
